profile.reading:
This facility sits at 17300 Highway 99, Lynnwood, Washington 98037, near Interstate 5 and close to Boeing's Everett manufacturing complex. Its OSM record labels it "SE1," but Csquare's own current Seattle-market page names the Lynnwood facility "SEA3," alongside two Tukwila sites, SEA1 and SEA2; "SE1" does not appear anywhere on Csquare's current site or SEC filings, so this profile treats SEA3 as the operator-confirmed code and flags "SE1" as a legacy or third-party label rather than resolving definitively which predecessor era it originates from. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's own spec page states 21,371 square feet of raised floor at SEA3, but its SEC Form S-1 property table gives a substantially larger figure, 37,843 square feet for "Seattle-SEA3_A," 76.1 percent leased and Csquare-owned as of March 31, 2026, a discrepancy of nearly double this profile flags rather than resolves. Csquare states 17.3 megawatts of utility power, 1.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 6 megawatts of generator capacity, with SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, ISO 27001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, and ENERGY STAR certifications, a broader environmental and safety-management certification set than Csquare lists for its other markets researched this session.

Lynnwood sits north of Seattle along the Highway 99/Interstate 5 corridor, near Paine Field and Boeing's Everett wide-body aircraft manufacturing complex, a submarket distinct from the Tukwila-area data center cluster south of Seattle where Csquare's SEA1 and SEA2 facilities sit. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, and the broader Seattle market has drawn substantial hyperscale and colocation investment over the past decade given the Pacific Northwest's relatively low-cost hydroelectric power and proximity to major submarine fiber cable landing points.

sources.title: Csquare, Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement

profile.research_note: Sqft is Csquare's own raised-floor figure for this single-building site (SEA3, OSM-tagged "SE1"); their SEC S-1 gives a nearly double 37,843 sqft "sellable" figure for the same building, a discrepancy Csquare's own materials do not explain -- flagged, not resolved.

reading.body:
Centersquare Lynnwood SE1, published as SEA3 in current Csquare branding, operates 17.3 megawatts of utility power supply in Lynnwood, north of Seattle along the Highway 99 corridor near Boeing's Everett manufacturing complex. At a typical 40 kW per rack for AI training workloads, this translates to roughly 430 racks as an assumption about density. The facility holds SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II certifications, PCI-DSS compliance, NIST 800-53 PE High qualification, and ISO 27001, 14001, and 45001 accreditation, positioning it to serve regulated enterprise and high-security tenants. An internal discrepancy exists between Csquare's stated 21,371 square feet of raised floor on its product page and 37,843 square feet reported in its SEC S-1 filing for the same building, which Csquare's own materials do not explain.

This facility ranks third by published capacity in Washington State, where only two of 46 mapped data center facilities publish power specifications, for a state total of 60 megawatts of disclosed IT load. SEA3 comprises 29 percent of that published figure and is one of three Csquare sites in the Seattle market, the other two located south in Tukwila. Csquare's full 64-facility portfolio across 21 markets published 389 megawatts of sellable capacity as of March 31, 2026, making this single Lynnwood site a roughly 4.4 percent slice of the operator's disclosed footprint.

The facility's backup infrastructure consists of 1.8 megawatts of UPS capacity and 6 megawatts of generator standby, sufficient to sustain roughly 105 racks on battery during utility loss and to support full-load runtime extensions via on-site generation. No total campus capacity figure or campus-level power ceiling was published. Ownership was verified as Csquare-controlled as of September 4, 2026.
